newsitem.title: USA: Ski resorts brace for airline strike.
newsitem.headline: Ski resorts brace for airline strike.

text.p: If American Airlines pilots go on strike Friday, it could not come at a worse time for Colorado's famed ski resorts, officials said.
"They're hoping for the best and preparing for the worst," said Lynn Bronikowski, spokeswoman for Colorado Ski Country USA, a trade group representing ski resorts.
The ski resorts have good reason to be nervous. Some 40 percent of their business comes between Presidents' Day weekend and the end of March.

Some 500,000 skier visits are expected for the upcoming holiday weekend alone. A skier visit is defined as one person on the slopes in a single day. The industry has about 11.2 million skier visits a year.

While UAL Corp.'s United Airlines has a 76 percent share of the traffic at Denver International Airport, AMR Corp's American Airlines has a number of flights that serve ski towns such as Crested Butte and Vail.
American accounts for 15 percent of the seats flying into Hayden, which serves the Steamboat Springs resort, and 12 percent of the seats to Crested Butte.

But the ski towns are not standing still. Resorts in Vail are making arrangements for more ground transportation to pick passengers up in Denver. Officials in Steamboat Springs contacted travelers and helped them change their flight plans.
Travelers with so-called electronic tickets on American Airlines were being advised to obtain a paper ticket, which would enable other carriers to honor their ticket.
Even a short delay in the start of a strike would not help the industry because the season runs to Easter. March is a popular month for skiing for students on spring break.

Colorado Ski Country President John Frew has asked Colorado's congressional delegation to support Republican Texas Sen. Kay Bailey Hutchison's request to President Clinton to intervene and prevent a strike if the two sides are unable to reach an accord.
Colorado accounts for 20 percent of the nation's $3.2 billion skiing business.
